messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Multigroup SEM doesn't converge
parts:
That is a lot of syntax to parse.
     The "lavaan did not run" message is pretty serious. I find that lavaan trundles right along, doing the best it can, even with fairly serious problems. Also, this is only a path model, so I would not see "model complexity" as the reason why it does not run. I am inclined to suspect a typo.
     You might consider using the "do.fit=F" option. I think lavaan will give you a framework for the output, which may help you to see how lavaan parsed your syntax. You did not get an error from the parser, but you still might have specified a different model than the one that you intended. That could be the core of your problem.
     I am intrigued by the warning that suggests you have non-ascii variable names in the failed syntax. You made many changes in the multigroup version, and it is possible that a typo crept in--but it is hard to pick out in the syntax.
     By removing some regressions from the second version, you did convert some variables to exogenous (by default) from endogenous. I don't think that is a key issue here, but you might try the suggestion of using the "fixed.x + F" option, just to check.
     Just ideas.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Multigroup SEM doesn't converge
parts:
ni...,
Ed has given you a lot of good suggestions.  Here are a few additional thoughts.

1. There are a number of online tools for removing non-ASCII characters from a file.

2. If there is indeed a convergence problem, you could try using the estimates from the single-group analysis as start values for the multiple-group analysis.  This assumes that they are scaled comparably.

3. Finally, my general suggestion for potential convergence problems is to fit the model to data generated the model in order to distinguish a model problem from a data problem.

Keith

ni...,
Ed has given you a lot of good suggestions.  Here are a few additional thoughts.

1. There are a number of online tools for removing non-ASCII characters from a file.

2. If there is indeed a convergence problem, you could try using the estimates from the single-group analysis as start values for the multiple-group analysis.  This assumes that they are scaled comparably.

3. Finally, my general suggestion for potential convergence problems is to fit the model to data generated the model in order to distinguish a model problem from a data problem.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Multigroup SEM doesn't converge
parts: You can have many endogenous categorical (ordinal) variables. Frequently, most or all observed variables are only ordinal, and lavaan churns right through that. I suspect that you "solved the problem" in passing. That is, the actual solution may have been accidentally achieved while trying to impose a different "solution."449 iterations for a path model seems like a lot, even with two groups, so I'm not sure that you have entirely dealt with the issue. If you want to look forther, I strongly suggest breaking your model down into pieces, and figuring out which pieces run well and which do not.
